correctness.rationale: Normalize an arbitrary nonzero real vector to sup norm one. Its signed active-set projective pattern lies in a ranked signed subset poset. If two patterns are comparable, a suitably signed small perturbation reduces one vector's norm strictly, contradicting directed Birkhoff–James orthogonality. Consequently a mutual-orthogonality clique injects into an antichain. A uniformly random coordinate permutation and independent signs generate a maximal chain hitting every rank-k projective pattern with probability 1/[C(n,k)2^(k-1)], proving the sharp LYM bound. For fixed k, all signed ternary support-k projective lines are pairwise mutually orthogonal, attaining it. Rank-size ratio 2(n-k)/(k+1) and binomial Stirling yield exact maximizing rank and asymptotic. Independently checked rank maxima n=1..16; checks are corroboration, not proof for arbitrary directions.
